data.turoyo: Ummo: "Gmandəmət. Gsulqono, gməblili aḥunonox, gṭorallox bu gubo. D solqət hat qamayto, lə kṭoratli, gguršatli.
data.translation: »Du wirst es bereuen; wenn ich hinaufsteige, so nehmen mich deine Brüder weg und lassen dich in der Cisterne; steigst du aber zuerst hinauf, so lassest du mich nicht hier, sondern ziehst mich hinauf«.

rationale: Thin III.1 Infectum cell: future regret with its practical reason supplied in context.

data.turoyo: W mandamla, məlla: "Ḥur! Ham ṭreli u taǧərawo w ham ste lawyono bu naṣib du abro d ʕammi! ʕAǧaba ḥal diḏi annaqqa mə gdowe?"
data.translation: Und sie bereute (was sie getan hatte,) und dachte: "Sieh! Den Kaufmann habe ich verlassen und meinem Vetter bin ich auch nicht zu Teil geworden! Was wird wohl jetzt aus mir werden?"

rationale: Thin III.1 Preterit cell: feminine experiencer and explicitly stated regretted choices.

data.turoyo: W hiya ste hawyo... mandamla ʕal u mede, d səmla.
data.translation: Sie aber bereut, was sie getan hat.

rationale: Thin III.1 Preterit cell: ʕal marks an explicit regretted action.

data.turoyo: Komər hano azzele məqdar ġalabe, haka ḥamməš, haka šeṯ əšne, lu ʕmiro səmle i beriye du greʕo w mandamle aʕle.
data.translation: Inzwischen verging lange Zeit, sei es fünf, sei es sechs Jahre, da bekam der Emir Sehnsucht nach seinem Knecht und bereute (, daß er ihn fortgejagt hatte).

rationale: Thin III.1 Preterit cell: personal ʕal complement and l-marked emir experiencer.

data.turoyo: Maqəmle an əstəloye mərle: “Gəd qəšʕina aṣ ṣəroye marke w gəd fašlan u malaṯṯe...“ Uʕdo Ǧamil Išler heš kəlle baḥ ḥaye, uʕdo kmandəm ʕal hayo ġalabe. <...>
data.translation: He roused the people of Astəl and said, “We will drive the Christians away from here, and their property will remain for us...” Now Jamil Ishler is still alive; now he regrets that very much. <...>

rationale: Thin Infectum cell has two after round 1; ongoing kmandəm with explicit ʕal stimulus and its antecedent. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation; the Turoyo determines the sense.

data.turoyo: I naqqa d kosom i ḥarbo, kowe ġalabe, komandam ġalabe w bəṯr... bəṯr b əšmo koṭoləb samaḥa. <...>
data.translation: When he does something wrong, he becomes very, he regrets it very much, and after... a little later he asks forgiveness. <...>

rationale: Thin Infectum cell; habitual wrongdoing-regret-apology sequence, with ko- and source a-vocalism retained. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation; the Turoyo determines the sense.

summary: All seven occurrences fit III.1 bereuen. No new lexical sense, stem, Detransitive box or idiom is supported.

l-series Preterit indexes the regret experiencer; the emir can also appear as an overt l-NP. ʕal introduces a person (26/221; 106/11) or the action regretted (78/207); content can instead be supplied by following speech.
Future g-Infectum predicts regret; bare d-Infectum rejects its possibility. Preterit mandamla can describe a current resultant regret state even where German uses present tense.
At 106/11 longing is separately expressed by səmle i beriye du greʕo; do not transfer a yearning meaning to mandamle.
All Jan tokens retain III.1 bereuen. ʕal hayo refers to a regretted action; the neighbouring ġabin pity expressions do not transfer a separate pity sense to ndm.
Infectum presents ongoing or habitual regret, whereas mandamle reports subsequent regret in a past sequence. Psychological meaning does not itself make active III Detransitive.

Experiencer is ordinary III subject; Preterit -le indexes that participant. New Infectum kmandəm/komandam supports the same sense without changing the inherited gloss or base forms. Preterit already has four examples after round 1, so its routine token is not added.
All 3 supplied occurrences were checked in input order, including repeated forms within one verse. Jan English is project machine translation; it is not independent semantic evidence.
Confirm that ʕal-person means regretting one’s treatment of that person, rather than a distinct “feel sorry for” use; current contexts support ordinary regret.
PrS 52/55 repeats inherited yaqəḏ lebe, mandamle at prs 147/26; verify edition numbering without silently changing the citation.
Does komandam beside kmandəm reflect regular reduced/unstressed vocalism or transcription variation? Retain both source spellings until checked.
